990-PF Part XV grants paid, direct from the NCCS e-file extracts

Source: R/efilepf.R
pf_efilepf.Rd

The grant file this project has matched against since the beginning is a GTDC Data Mart extract (2025_08_29_All_Years_990PFPart14Grants3A.csv, 12,559,051 rows, tax years 2008-2024). This module rebuilds the same table from the NCCS e-file extracts instead, which is the upstream source and is both larger and fresher.

Usage

pf_efilepf_years()

pf_efilepf_table()

pf_efilepf_dir()

Why rebuild

Measured against the inventory the bucket publishes alongside the data:

sourcerowstax years
GTDC Part14Grants3A12,559,0512008-2024
e-file PF-P15-T0117,560,7672009-2025

That is 5.0M more grant rows (+40%) and an additional year. The e-file extract is also regenerated continuously, so a rebuild is reproducible on demand rather than pinned to whenever the Data Mart extract was cut.

Which version, and the trap

Use efilepf_v3_1. efilepf_v2_3 exists in the same bucket and carries the same PF-* table family, but its published row inventory reports zero rows for PF-P15-T01 in every year — the grants-paid table is not populated there. This is the same shape of trap as efile_v2_1 vs efile_v2_2 for Schedule I (see pf_schedi_url()), where the superseded extract carried the right schema and a tenth of the rows. Always check COUNT-OF-ROWS-BY-TABLE-AND-FORMTYPE-*.CSV before trusting a version.

Part XIV or Part XV

The GTDC file is named "Part14" and this table "P15". They are the same schedule: grants and contributions paid during the year. The IRS renumbered the 990-PF supplementary-information part, and the e-file extracts follow the current numbering. PF-P15-T01 is the repeating grant-level table; PF-P15-T00 is the one-row-per-return parent; PF-P15-T02 is grants approved for future payment, which is a different population and is not what this project matches.

2025 drops the recipient-status column

PF_15_G_PAID_RECIP_STAT – the GTDC SIGOCPYRFSTA, "foundation status of recipient" – is present every year 2009-2024 and absent from 2025. One column removed; the other 29 are identical. The IRS revised Form 990-PF and dropped that box from Part XV line 3, so this is permanent and 2026 onward will not have it either.

It matters more than a missing field normally would, because pf_standardize_status() reads it and it is the only input to the scope decision. Measured rather than assumed: with the column absent every row classifies as other_unknown and in_scope stays TRUE, because the recipient-type filter flags individuals and government bodies rather than dropping them and only a foreign address removes a row. So 2025 grants are matched normally; what is lost is the ability to crosstab them by recipient type, and any such breakdown must exclude 2025 or report it separately rather than showing a year that is 100% other_unknown and letting a reader conclude the data is broken.

Column naming

pf_efilepf_build() emits the GTDC column names, not the e-file ones. That is deliberate: pf_prepare_grants() reads SIGOCPYRBNBN1, SIGOCPYRFSTA and friends by name, as do the recipient-type and scope rules, so emitting the historical schema means the entire downstream pipeline, every benchmark and every frozen artifact keeps working untouched. pf_efilepf_map() is the mapping, exported so the translation is auditable rather than buried.
